title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 22
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: What fraction of a day is 108 minutes?
questions.explanation: A day holds 1,440 minutes, so 108 minutes is 108/1,440. Dividing top and bottom by 36 leaves 3/40. 9/120 and 27/360 are the same number but not in lowest terms, and 1/12 would be 120 minutes rather than 108.

questions.prompt: What is the positive solution of x² + 2x − 35 = 0?
questions.explanation: Two numbers multiplying to −35 and adding to 2 are 7 and −5, so the equation factorises as (x + 7)(x − 5) = 0 and the solutions are -7 and 5. The positive one is 5. -7 is the other root, and 7 is the factor rather than the solution — the sign flips when the bracket is set to zero.

questions.prompt: What is the mean of all the whole numbers from 17 to 43 inclusive?
questions.explanation: Consecutive numbers are evenly spaced, so their mean is the average of the first and last: (17 + 43) / 2 = 30. 27 is how many numbers there are and 26 is the gap between the ends — neither is the average.

questions.prompt: A person 1.8 m tall casts a shadow 2.4 m long. At the same moment a tree casts a shadow 20 m long. How tall is the tree?
questions.explanation: The sun's angle is the same for both, so height and shadow are in proportion: 1.8 / 2.4 = 0.75. Applying that to the 20 m shadow gives 15 m. Dividing the wrong way round gives 26.67 m, a tree far taller than its shadow when the person is shorter than theirs.

questions.prompt: If a : b is 2 : 3 and b : c is 4 : 5, what is a : c?
questions.explanation: To join the two ratios, b must read the same in both. Scaling a : b by 4 gives 8 : 12, and scaling b : c by 3 gives 12 : 15. So a : b : c is 8 : 12 : 15, and a : c is 8 : 15. Reading the outer numbers straight off gives 2 : 5, which ignores that b means different things in the two ratios.

questions.prompt: How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 are divisible by 3 or by 5?
questions.explanation: 33 are divisible by 3 and 20 by 5, but 6 are divisible by both and have been counted twice. Taking those off gives 33 + 20 − 6 = 47. Adding the two counts without subtracting the overlap gives 53.

questions.prompt: Two people are chosen at random. Assuming birthdays fall equally often in each of the 12 months, what is the probability that both were born in the same month?
questions.explanation: The first person's month can be anything. The second must match it, and one month in 12 does, so the probability is 1/12. 1/144 would be the chance of both being born in one particular named month, which is a stricter requirement than simply matching.

questions.prompt: A photograph 20 cm by 15 cm has a border 2 cm wide all the way round, inside those measurements. What area does the border cover?
questions.explanation: The picture inside the border measures 16 cm by 11 cm, an area of 176 cm², against 300 cm² in all. The border is the difference: 124 cm². Taking only 2 cm off each dimension rather than 4 gives 66 cm² and forgets the border runs along both sides.

questions.prompt: A train 150 m long travelling at 54 km/h overtakes a walker going the same way at 9 km/h. How long does the train take to pass the walker completely?
questions.explanation: Going the same way, the speeds subtract: 54 − 9 = 45 km/h, which is 12.5 m/s. The train covers its own 150 m relative to the walker in 12 seconds. Adding the speeds gives 8.57 seconds and would apply if they were moving towards each other.

questions.prompt: A tank measures 80 cm by 50 cm by 40 cm and holds 96 litres of water. What percentage of its capacity is that?
questions.explanation: The tank's capacity is 160,000 cm³, and a litre is 1,000 cm³, so it holds 160 litres when full. 96 of 160 is 60%. The conversion is the step to watch: a tank measured in centimetres gives a capacity in cubic centimetres, not litres.

questions.prompt: Solve for x: 12 / (x − 3) = 4
questions.explanation: Multiplying both sides by (x − 3) gives 12 = 4(x − 3), so x − 3 = 3 and x = 6. 3 is the value of the bracket rather than of x — the 3 still has to be added back.

questions.prompt: Buses leave every 18 minutes, the first at 06:00. How many leave between 06:00 and 09:00, counting both?
questions.explanation: Three hours is 180 minutes, which holds 10 gaps of 18 minutes. Counting the 06:00 departure as well as the 10 that follow gives 11 buses. 10 counts the gaps rather than the buses, which is the fence-post error in timetable form.

questions.prompt: 7 books cost £52.85. At the same price each, what do 12 books cost?
questions.explanation: One book costs £52.85 / 7 = £7.55, so 12 cost £90.60. Dividing by 12 and multiplying by 7 reverses the proportion and gives £30.83, less money for more books.

questions.prompt: A quantity is halved, and the result is halved again. By what percentage has the original been reduced?
questions.explanation: Halving twice leaves a quarter of the original, or 25%, so 75% has gone. 50% is the effect of a single halving, and adding two halvings to make 100% would leave nothing at all.

questions.prompt: A survey records: 2 appears 5 times, 3 appears 8 times, 4 appears 4 times, 5 appears 3 times. What is the mean?
questions.explanation: The 20 readings total 2 × 5 + 3 × 8 + 4 × 4 + 5 × 3 = 65, so the mean is 65 / 20 = 3.25. Averaging the four distinct values without their frequencies gives 3.5 and treats a value seen 8 times as no more important than one seen 3 times.

questions.prompt: What is the height of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm, in surd form?
questions.explanation: Dropping a perpendicular splits the triangle into two right-angled halves with a base of 5 cm and a hypotenuse of 10 cm. The height is the square root of 10² − 5² = 75, which is 5√3 cm. 25√3 cm² would be the area, not the height.

questions.prompt: A representative is paid £1,800.00 a month plus £45.00 for each sale above 20. What is the pay in a month with 34 sales?
questions.explanation: Only the 34 − 20 = 14 sales above the threshold earn a bonus: 14 × £45.00 = £630.00, on top of the £1,800.00. Paying a bonus on all 34 sales gives £3,330.00 and ignores the threshold.

questions.prompt: Two numbers multiply to 864 and have a highest common factor of 12. What is their lowest common multiple?
questions.explanation: For any two numbers, the highest common factor times the lowest common multiple equals their product: 12 × LCM = 864, so the LCM is 72. The pair 24 and 36 fits — they multiply to 864, share a factor of 12, and have 72 as their lowest common multiple.

questions.prompt: A debt is charged interest at 1.5% a month, compounded. What is the equivalent annual rate, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Twelve months of compounding multiply the debt by 1.015 to the twelfth power, which is 1.1956 — an annual rate of 19.56%. Multiplying the monthly rate by twelve gives 18% and leaves out the interest charged on interest.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of the sequence 4, 9, 14, …?
questions.explanation: The 20th term is 4 + 19 × 5 = 99. The sum of an evenly spaced run is the number of terms times the average of the first and last: 20 × (4 + 99) / 2 = 1,030. 99 is the last term on its own, and 1,980 multiplies every term up to the largest.

questions.prompt: A coach costs £480.00 to hire plus £6.00 for each passenger. With 40 passengers, what does each pay if the whole cost is shared equally?
questions.explanation: The hire works out at £480.00 / 40 = £12.00 a head, and each passenger also costs £6.00, giving £18.00 each. The whole trip costs £720.00, which divided by 40 comes to the same £18.00.
